prompt: Which tiny creature carries its spiral home on its back?
hint: Look for a slimy friend with a swirl shell.

fact.text: Snails can nap for up to three whole years if the weather is too dry!

prompt: Who works in a buzzing team to make sweet golden honey?
hint: They buzz around flowers and wear yellow-black stripes.

fact.text: Honeybees dance in waggle shapes to tell friends where sweet flowers grow.

prompt: Tap all the animals that can flutter across the green meadow!
hint: Look for wings that flutter in the air.

fact.text: Butterflies taste sweet flower nectar using tiny sensors on their feet!

prompt: Tap all the crunchy snacks you can harvest from a garden!
hint: Pick the crunchy root and sweet red berry.

fact.text: Strawberries are the only fruit wearing their seeds on the outside!

prompt: Order how a sunny plant grows from seed to blossom!
hint: Start with the seed, then sprout, then bloom.

fact.text: Young sunflowers turn their happy faces across the sky to follow sunlight.

prompt: Order these meadow critters from smallest to biggest size!
hint: Ant is tiny, frog is medium, fox is large.

fact.text: Ants can lift heavy pebbles fifty times bigger than their own bodies!

prompt: Which giant glowing star warms our planet Earth every single day?
hint: It shines in the daytime and gives us warm golden light.

fact.text: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to zoom all the way to Earth!

prompt: Which dusty silver friend glows bright in our dark night sky?
hint: Look for the crescent companion that visits when you sleep.

fact.text: The moon has zero wind, so astronaut footprints last for millions of years!

prompt: Tap all the icy wonders that fall down from stormy clouds!
hint: Choose the wet rain drop and cold snowflake.

fact.text: Every single falling snowflake forms with six delicate crystal arms in the clouds.

prompt: Tap all the glowing lights that sparkle high in the sky!
hint: Pick the twinkling night star and colorful arch.

fact.text: Rainbows form complete circles, but we usually see only the top half arc.

prompt: Order the sky from cheerful morning sunrise to dark starry night!
hint: Start with dawn, then noon, then bedtime.

fact.text: Earth spins once every twenty-four hours to make day turn into night.

prompt: Order these sky wonders from closest to ground to farthest away!
hint: Clouds float nearby, moon is further, stars are deep in space.

fact.text: The closest twinkling night star is trillions of miles away from us.

prompt: Which amazing organ beats like a drum inside your chest?
hint: It goes thump-thump to keep you running and jumping.

fact.text: Your heart beats about one hundred thousand times every single energetic day!

prompt: Which clever boss inside your head thinks and creates great ideas?
hint: It helps you solve puzzles, dream, and remember stories.

fact.text: Your brain makes enough electrical energy to power a small glowing lightbulb!

prompt: Tap all the sensory helpers on your cheerful smiling face!
hint: Pick the eyes for seeing and nose for smelling.

fact.text: Your amazing nose can recognize more than fifty thousand different pleasant smells!

prompt: Tap all the healthy choices that make your bones grow strong!
hint: Select nutritious milk and deep sleep.

fact.text: Drinking fresh milk and getting rest helps bones build sturdy calcium frames.

prompt: Order your morning routine from waking up to heading out!
hint: Wake up first, wash hands and face, then grab your bag.

fact.text: A morning stretch brings fresh oxygen to your muscles so you feel awake!

prompt: Order enjoying a snack from first chew to running fast!
hint: Take the apple, chew it well, then go zoom outside.

fact.text: Your tummy converts wholesome food into fuel that powers your running legs!
